q.intro.text: An x by x square and a strip six wide and x long: together, x squared plus six x equals sixteen. Which numbers make that true? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.right.text: At the start you picked two and negative eight, and you were right. Now you can show why: fill the corner on both sides, then take both roots.

q.cb.one.text: At the start you picked one and negative seven. That adds the nine to the left side only. Both sides get the nine.

q.cb.pos.text: At the start you picked two only. But negative five squares to twenty-five too, so negative eight is a solution as well.

q.cb.none.text: Fill the corner on both sides, read the square, take both roots. That is completing the square.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the equation.

e.step0.text: The strip of six x splits into two strips of three x. One turns under the square. Same area, but now it is a square with one corner missing.

e.step1.text: The missing corner is three by three: nine. Fill it in, and add nine to the other side too, or the two sides stop being equal.

e.step2.text: The whole is now one square with side x plus three. So x plus three, squared, equals twenty-five.

e.step3.text: Both five and negative five square to twenty-five. So x plus three is five, or x plus three is negative five: x equals two, or x equals negative eight. Both check.

e.why.text: Quick check: why are there two solutions?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. A positive number has two square roots, and each one gives a solution.

e.why.pos.text: The picture is a helper; the equation is about numbers. Put negative eight in: sixty-four minus forty-eight is sixteen. It works.

e.why.always.text: Not always. If the right side were zero there would be one, and if it were negative, none.

t.intro.text: Now x squared plus eight x equals nine. The strip is split for you.

t.corner.text: The missing corner is four by four. What number do you add to both sides?

t.corner.ok.text: Yes: sixteen. Add it on the left to fill the corner, and on the right to keep the balance.

t.corner.no.text: Half of eight is four, the side of the corner. Its area is four times four.

t.corner.side.text: Four is the side of the corner. You add its area, four times four.

t.corner.b.text: Halve the eight first, then square: four times four.

t.right.text: So x plus four, squared, equals what? What is the right side?

t.right.ok.text: Yes: x plus four, squared, equals twenty-five.

t.right.no.text: The right side was nine. Add the sixteen to it.

t.right.one.text: Sixteen went into the left side, so it goes into the right side too: nine plus sixteen.

t.right.drop.text: Keep the nine that was there: nine plus sixteen.

t.roots.text: x plus four is five, or x plus four is negative five. Type both solutions.

t.roots.h.text: Five and negative five are the values of x plus four. Take four off each.

t.roots.one.text: There are two square roots of twenty-five: five and negative five. Each gives a solution.

t.roots.sign.text: x plus four equals five means x equals five minus four. Subtract the four.

t.roots.no.text: x plus four is five, or x plus four is negative five. Solve each.

t.roots.ok.text: Yes: x equals one, or x equals negative nine. Check: one plus eight is nine, and eighty-one minus seventy-two is nine.

p.intro.text: Lee says: the quadratic formula is a separate rule to memorize. It has nothing to do with completing the square. Complete the square on a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero, and see. Is Lee right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Complete the square on the general equation, and see where it leads.

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.no.some.text: Every term is divided by a, or the equation changes. That is the slip that leaves b instead of b over a.

p.no.half.text: After dividing by a, the x coefficient is b over a. Half of that is b over two a.

p.no.split.text: A square root does not split over a minus sign. The root stays whole.

p.no.other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.c1.text: Right. Dividing by a makes the square an x by x square again, and the constant moves across.

p.c2.text: Right. The strip of b over a x splits in two, and the corner is b over two a, squared. Both sides get it.

p.c3.text: Right. The left side is the big square. The right side over four a squared is b squared minus four a c.

p.c4.text: Right. Both roots, then subtract b over two a. That is the quadratic formula.

p.done.text: That is a proof: the quadratic formula is completing the square, done once with letters. Lee is wrong.
